paper.title: Hierarchical Adversarial Bandits for Online Configuration Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Nonstochastic MAB with arbitrary partition of arms into clusters (finite AL-MAB)
unmapped: the learner is given a partition of the K arms into p clusters (arbitrary, no metric assumed)
settings.definition_quote: The problem instance is a triple $(K , \cD, \cC)$, where $K$ is the set of $k$ arms ... $\cC$ is an expected rewards assignment, i.e., an infinite sequence $\mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2,...$ of vectors ... $\mathbf{c}_t : K \rightarrow [0, 1]$ ... In this subsection, we study the regret where the partition (or clustering) is done arbitrarily, i.e., without assuming any metric between the arms.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial Lipschitz MAB (finite) with an l-partition
unmapped: finite set of K arms in a metric space; reward vector c_t is 1-Lipschitz w.r.t. the metric at every round
the learner is given a partition of arms into p clusters, each of diameter at most l (l-partition)
settings.definition_quote: An arms partition $\cP$ is an $\ell$-partition if the following Lipschitz condition holds: $\forall P \in \cP, a,b \in P, \vert c_t(a)-c_t(b) \vert \le \mathcal{D}(a,b) \le \ell, \forall$ rounds $t$.

symbols.p: number of clusters in the partition
symbols.k_star: size of the cluster containing the best arm in hindsight

conditions: arbitrary partition of the arms into p clusters
tuning: EXP3 used at both parent and child levels

source.label: thm:clusters
source.quote: For $k$ nonstochastic arms, $T>0$ and a partition $\cP$ of the arms, the regret of the \EXP32 algorithm using EXP3 is bounded as follows: G_{\max} - \exp[G_{\EXP32}] \le \cO(\sqrt{p T \log p }) + \cO(\sqrt{k^* T \log k^*}) +\cO(\sqrt{k T \log (k/p)}) where $p$ is the number of clusters and $k^*$ is the size of the cluster with the best arm in hindsight.

results.notes: Built from Claim 6.1 components. Regret G_max - E[G_A] with c_t expected rewards. Horizon knowledge not stated explicitly; standard EXP3 tuning uses T.

symbols.k_star: size of the cluster containing the best arm in hindsight
symbols.ell: maximum within-cluster distance of the l-partition

source.label: cor:weakLip
source.quote: For $k$ nonstochastic arms, $T>0$ and an $\ell$-partition $\cP$ of the arms, the regret of the \EXP32 algorithm using EXP3 is bounded as follows: G_{\max} - \exp[G_{\EXP32}] \le \cO(\sqrt{p T \log p }) + \cO(\sqrt{k^* T \log k^*}) + T \cdot \ell

results.notes: The T*ell term is stated exactly (not in O) in the paper; recorded under overall O notation.

symbols.k_star: size of the cluster containing the best arm in hindsight
symbols.ell: maximum within-cluster distance of the l-partition

conditions: the child algorithm ALB+ satisfies Property 1: regret O(ell*sqrt(k' T log k')) on a cluster of k' arms with maximum distance ell (e.g. EXP3-SET with side-information feedback graph with independence number <= ell^2 k')

source.label: thm:ClustersLipschitz
source.quote: For $k$ nonstochastic arms, $T>0$ and an $\ell$-partition $\cP$ of the arms, the regret of the \EXP32, using an ALB$^+$ algorithm can be bounded as follows: G_{\max} - \exp[G_{\EXP32}] \le \cO(\sqrt{p T \log p }) +\cO(\ell \sqrt{k^* T \log k^*}) +\cO(\ell \cdot \sqrt{k T \log (k/p) })

results.notes: Conditional on existence of an ALB+ algorithm (Property 1), which in the paper's example requires side-information feedback, not pure bandit feedback.

bound.regime: ell <= K^(-1/4), p = sqrt(K) clusters each of size sqrt(K)

symbols.ell: maximum within-cluster distance of the l-partition

conditions: sqrt(K) clusters each of size sqrt(K)

source.quote: Given an $\ell$-partition $\cP$, with $\ell \le \frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{k}}$ and $\sqrt{k}$ clusters, each of size $\sqrt{k}$, the \EXP32, using an ALB$^+$ algorithm can be bounded as $\cO(\sqrt{k^{1/2} T \log k})$, which is $\Omega(\sqrt[4]{k})$ time better than the flat ALB$^+$ algorithm.
